title: 2023 HMMT November Guts Problem 19
statement:
Suppose \(a, b\), and \(c\) are real numbers such that

\[\begin{aligned}
a^{2}-b c & =14 \\
b^{2}-c a & =14, \text { and } \\
c^{2}-a b & =-3
\end{aligned}\]

Compute \(|a+b+c|\).

solutions.text:
Subtracting the first two equations gives \((a-b)(a+b+c)=0\), so either \(a=b\) or \(a+b+c=0\). However, subtracting first and last equations gives \((a-c)(a+b+c)=17\), so \(a+b+c \neq 0\). This means \(a=b\).

Now adding all three equations gives \((a-c)^{2}=25\), so \(a-c= \pm 5\). Then \(a+b+c= \pm \frac{17}{5}\).
